title: Accounting for a Trading Business: CRJ and CPJ
summary: How a trading business differs from a service business, trading stock, mark-up and cost of sales, and recording cash sales and purchases in the CRJ and CPJ.

notes.text: A **service business** earns income by providing a service (a hair salon, a plumber). A **trading business** buys goods (called **trading stock**) and sells them at a higher price to make a profit (a clothing shop, a spaza shop).

rows: Goods bought to sell again; an asset
Income from selling trading stock, at selling price
The cost price of the goods that were sold; an expense
The amount (usually a percentage of cost price) added to the cost to get the selling price

notes.title: Finding the cost of sales
notes.problem: A shop uses a mark-up of 50% on cost. It sells goods for R1 800 cash. Calculate the cost of sales.

notes.label: Remember
notes.text: Every time goods are sold, **two things happen**: the business earns **sales** (income at selling price) and loses **trading stock** (an asset, at cost price). That is why the CRJ of a trading business has both a Sales column and a Cost of sales column.

notes.title: From cost price to selling price
notes.problem: A shop buys a kettle for R80 and adds a mark-up of 50% on cost. Calculate the selling price and the gross profit.
steps: The gross profit on the kettle is the mark-up.
notes.answer: Selling price R120; gross profit R40.
